title: Hawthorn Labs: Quicklaunch & Hosting Options - Discovery
next_steps: Send security packet and SOC2 summary (Maya)
Enable $5k free credit in trial account (Maya)
Schedule 30m benchmark run with 10k prompt set (Liam)
Share estimated pricing for dedicated pilot (Maya)
action_items: Maya: Send SOC 2 + KMS docs by 2027-12-06
Liam: Spin up benchmark runner, test 8k context model + quantized variant by 2027-12-08
Evelyn: Share expected QPS and peak concurrency numbers by 2027-12-07
summary: Initial discovery for Hawthorn Labs evaluating Redwood for dev-facing quicklaunch. Main concerns: time-to-first-token, free credits for prototype, hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC), and security (KMS/SOC2). Agreed to a short benchmark pilot and share security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I see Evelyn, Samir, Jordan — welcome. We're gonna run through how to get Hawthorn to first token quickly and then dig into hosting options.
[00:12] Evelyn (Hawthorn CTO): Thanks Maya, yeah we wanna get something in front of product teams in two weeks ideally. Budget's small at first, so free credits and a fast path are key.
[00:22] Samir (Head of ML): Quick note — we care about privacy; we may need VPC or private later. Also curious about latency at 500ms p95 for chat use case.
[00:31] Liam (Redwood SE): Cool, good constraints. On the self-serve side our Redwood API quicklaunch can get you to first token in under an hour for straightforward requests, w/ our free credit allocation. For latency, hosted tiers typically do 150–400ms p95 on smaller models, dedicated can tighten that.
[00:50] Jordan (Eng Manager): When you say "first token in under an hour" like literally? We want engineers to try it in a sprint.
[00:57] Maya (Redwood AE): Yeah literally — signup, API key, sample prompts, SDKs. We'll provision a trial org and give you credits. That covers experiments without going through procurement.
[01:10] Samir: And if we hit rate limits or need guaranteed throughput, what's the path?
[01:16] Liam: The typical path is start hosted self-serve. If you need predictable throughput, switch to Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with autoscale and SLAs. Private is for when you need VPC or on-prem for compliance.
[01:29] Evelyn: What's the overhead for Dedicated — like commitment and lead time?
[01:34] Maya: For pilots we have short-term reserved pilots, usually a month min for a dedicated node, but we can do a short pilot with burst capacity. I'll share the dedicated pricing grid.
[01:44] Jordan: I'm worried about keys and data — can we bring our own KMS?
[01:48] Liam: Yes — Private deployments integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Hosted supports envelope encryption and customer-managed keys in some regions; we'll include specifics in the security packet.
[01:59] Samir: Another big one: do you keep logs or token content? We need auditability but not long retention.
[02:06] Maya: By default hosted keeps minimal logs for billing; you can opt out or set retention. Audit logs are available for Dedicated/Private with longer retention under enterprise plans.
[02:18] [Speaker 2]: there was a quick interruption there — sorry —
[02:22] Liam: No worries. On the model side we have a model catalog with verified performance profiles. For a 8k-context LLM we have quantized variants that reduce cost and still hit reasonable latency.
[02:38] Evelyn: How easy is model swapping — say we want to switch from a smaller model during alpha to a larger one for prod?
[02:44] Liam: You can pin model versions and rollout via canary or A/B in the console; runtime handles KV cache and graceful fallbacks if a model is down.
[02:55] Samir: Latency vs cost tradeoffs — any typical numbers?
[02:59] Liam: Roughly put, hosted smaller models: lower cost, slightly higher variance in p95; dedicated with pinned quantization: lower variance and lower per-token cost at scale. Batching and prefix caching reduce cost but can increase tail latency if you wait for batches. We can tune autoscaling policies per route.
[03:22] Jordan: For our case it's interactive chat so we need <500ms p95 ideally.
[03:27] Liam: We should benchmark your workload — streaming responses improve perceived latency too; we'll run a test with your prompt set.
[03:34] Evelyn: What's the onboarding for product folks — do we need an SE?
[03:38] Maya: For quickstart we provide docs and SDKs. AE and an SE can do a 30–60 minute live walkthrough. For the pilot we'll have Liam oversee the benchmark.
[03:49] Samir: About security review — procurement will want SOC2, data flow diagrams, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, encryption.
[03:58] Maya: Yep that's standard. I'll include SSO docs, SOC 2 report summary, and how audit logs and KMS work.
[04:06] [00:04:12] Jordan: Do you support VPC peering or private endpoints?
[04:16] Liam: Yes — Private deployment supports private endpoints and VPC peering; hosted supports VPC endpoints in select regions. For on-prem there's an air-gapped package.
[04:25] Evelyn: Any gotchas around data residency? We operate in EU primarily.
[04:30] Maya: We have EU regions and can run Private control plane options; we'll note that in the packet.
[04:36] Samir: Regarding cost — can you give a back-of-envelope?
[04:39] Liam: Off the cuff, for small prototyping with quantized models you'd be in the low cents per 1k tokens; dedicated units at scale drop that considerably. But I'll do a tailored estimate after we see the QPS and token mix.
[04:53] Maya: For now we can enable an account with $5k dev credits so teams can run experiments; then we'll run the benchmark to estimate committed capacity.
[05:02] Jordan: That sounds good. One procedural question — how do we escalate if we hit quality regressions after model updates?
[05:08] Liam: We have eval hooks and rollback/automatic fallback policies — you can tie regressions to prompt-eval suites and be alerted on drift.
[05:18] Samir: Perfect. Also we'll want to test streaming and function/tool calling for a retrieval use case.
[05:25] Liam: Yep supported — function calling and structured outputs are part of the API. We can include example retrieval pipelines in the sample repo.
[05:34] [00:05:35] Evelyn: On the org side, are there RBAC roles for dev vs ops?
[05:39] Maya: Yes, console supports roles and SSO provisioning; we can demo that in the follow-up.
[05:44] Jordan: For the pilot benchmark, what inputs do you need from us?
[05:48] Liam: A sample of typical prompts (10k ideally but smaller sets ok), expected concurrency/peak QPS, and the desired latency SLO.
[05:56] Samir: We'll compile a representative prompt set — some will be retrieval-augmented, some pure chat.
[06:03] Maya: Great. I'll send a quick checklist for the benchmark.
[06:07] [00:06:08] Liam: Quick aside — competitors? They asked about OpenAI and Cohere earlier; our differentiators are the unified runtime, predictable dedicated capacity, and private deployment options plus cost controls.
[06:22] Evelyn: Do you have any reference customers in healthcare — we have one foot in regulated data?
[06:27] Maya: We do; I can redact and share case studies and compliance scoping notes.
[06:33] Jordan: For the dev flow, are there client SDKs?
[06:36] Liam: Yes — Python, Node, and Java SDKs with examples, plus a Postman collection.
[06:41] Samir: About rollout, we'd want a canary traffic policy to slowly move from hosted to dedicated if needed.
[06:47] Liam: That's supported; you can define route-level policies and fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is exhausted.
[06:56] [00:06:57] Evelyn: Let's talk timeline — we want a working prototype in two weeks and then a pilot in six weeks. Is that realistic?
[07:05] Maya: Yes, two weeks for a prototype on hosted with credits is very doable. Dedicated pilot in six weeks is possible depending on the contract cadence; we'll aim for a pilot start around then.
[07:16] Jordan: Any required legal hoops before we get credits?
[07:19] Maya: The trial credits can be applied after basic T&Cs acceptance; full enterprise contracts only for Dedicated/Private.
[07:25] Samir: For the benchmark, can you show live latency graphs and token cost breakdown?
[07:30] Liam: Absolutely — Redwood Console offers token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency dashboards, and trace hooks. We'll include screenshots.
[07:39] Evelyn: Ok, I think that's enough to move forward. Could you confirm the next steps?
[07:44] Maya: Sure — I'll send the security packet and enable $5k credits; Liam will schedule the benchmark and share the runner instructions; Evelyn will send QPS + prompt set.
[07:55] [00:07:56] Jordan: And we'll aim to have the prompt set in 3 business days.
[08:00] Maya: Great, we'll follow up in email with times for the benchmark next week. Thanks everyone.
[08:07] Samir: Thank you.
[08:09] [End of recording]
